decisions.reason: The repellent chain was the wall in both long runs. The Southern Shore and its dark passage now say no light crosses the lake and that what keeps a grue off is sold in a can in a room with an eight on its wall that the table shows, and the table's Room 8 image names the spray can; the lair itself and the five-move spray are the original's and unchanged.
Reaching the end of Q2 was the round's progress; the trap on the aqueduct stays, as the brief's faithfulness asks, but the visitor now walks into it told (see P8). The repellent chain is P1's.

Replayed goal-seeker-1 to t97-99: the amulet was taken and then scattered by the drowning in the same turn, and the inventory line, rendered after the turn's work, read the hands the old man had already emptied. Not a Sprout bug; the death's waking line now says what became of what was carried, and the sand's glint reads whether the shiny thing is still there. Logged under friction 3's note.

The loss is kept, as recommended; the three shores now tell a visitor who returns carrying a lit light what the water does to it, in brief mode too, and the Western Shore says no light crosses from either side and the far dark is got through another way.

Shout, shout for help, hello and who is there at the ledge are answered in the man's voice by stage, through the visitor's own parts since the ledge's stand-in cannot hear a bare shout: a chuckle before he shows, his promise while away, 'grab the rope' when back, silence once gone; at the top with him there, a wince. 'man, who are you?' is the no-addressee decision, logged in friction 38/39's status.

The wait while he is away is a sequence keyed on the moves he has left (the lock tried, the coins counted, the pacing, the footsteps back to the brink); the timing is the original's ten moves, untouched.
The lean toward the hand stays for views I to III, which it was written for; for the altar the surface 'seems content to be looked at', so the trap rests on the image as the original's does.

After the quake the Key Room's description and its cover carry a draught and the smell of open air, the cover examined says the channel below has lost a piece to the chasm, and the Aqueduct's own description says the channel stops against the air to the north. The one-way drop is the original's and stays.

The remainder-dropping is Sprout's and is added to friction 38/39's status and to friction 48 for overstory-social/sprout; in the world the common forms are read whole: shout hello/up/for help as a shout, say hello, sailor as a greeting, wait N as one move said in character, sleep and rest as waits.
DIAGNOSE's second line is restored ('You will be cured after N moves.'), and sleep, rest, nap and wait a while are waits; the duel's odds are the original's and are left alone, as recommended.

pull back hood and its kin reach the hood; every shadow room has the mist the brief names; bare search reads the room; feel around is answered in the dark and out of it; dry lamp says the lake got in where drying does not reach; climb stair has one answer (a composed play needed a without, friction 47).
The rule is the original's NO-OBJS and stays; the refusal now says the passageway takes nothing bigger than a hand, the light included, so the next ride can be tried empty-handed.
Log only: the altar is added to friction 24's status beside the Prison Cell, for Sprout's test reporter; the world cannot and should not change it.
No change to the window, which is the original's one command; the sailing line now says, after the fact, that he had been listening for something and it was not said.
The wait at the Vista reads the world's indicator clock: the image lies quiet, stirs, and goes thin as the change nears. The clock is unchanged.

changes.what: By the brief's schedule, built Q3 whole: the Tight Squeeze, Crystal Grotto, Royal Hall and Great Door with the earthquake's cleft; the Museum Entrance, Jewel Room (cage, pedestal, Crown Jewels, plaque, robot) and Technology Museum (grey, black and gold machines, plaque) in the present, in the years between and in 776 with the guards outside the door, Lord Flathead's voice and the jewels on a bare pedestal; one door of each kind standing in every year; the Creepy Crawl's way east opened onto the Tight Squeeze; the quake felt at the Great Door; death scatters to the Tight Squeeze too.

By the brief's schedule, built the time machine: the gold machine as a place a visitor sits in, pushed room to room by a value role over the compass and following its pusher through the gate, damaged over the stairs or the cleft, carried home by the robot; the dial set by an integer role, the seat with the ring's hollow, the button that sends the sitter to the dial's year (the point at 776; the stone death before 776; the dedication and the guards before 883; the same room in later years; the present with the cleft filled in past 948), possessions left in the room, the doors shut, the forty-move snap back, the guards' clock, the robbery judged on leaving 776 and the present rewritten (cage, jewels, plaque, descriptions).

By the brief's schedule, built the Royal Puzzle: the entrance with its warning note and hole, the Side Room with the steel door and slot, and the Room in a Puzzle as 36 generated squares over a world-held grid from the original's table, with the four walls and the ladder one thing each in every square; pushing a wall (the sixth point, the legend once), the map drawn as three rows of prose, diagonal steps past a corner, objects snapped to the Side Room, the hole blocked by a wall pushed under it, the good ladder out, the book in its niche and the slot that takes it as the exit fee.

The repellent chain told: the Southern Shore's description and its dark passage (and the shared passage presence there) say no light crosses the lake and that what keeps a grue off is a can in the room with the eight that the table shows; the table's Room 8 image names the spray can.

The fallen arch told from the Key Room side: after the quake the room's description, the manhole cover's description and the Aqueduct's own description carry the draught, the smell of open air and the channel that stops against the air to the north; the Key Room hears the quake as a grinding below the cover.
The death's waking line says what was carried is lying along the way in with the lamp alone brought back; the lake sand's search line reads whether the shiny thing is still there.

The Lake Shore, Western Shore and Southern Shore tell a visitor who returns carrying a lit light that the water takes it, in brief mode too; the Western Shore's description says no light crosses from either side.
Shouts, hellos and 'who is there' at the ledge and the cliff top answered in the man's voice by his stage; an intent reads 'shout for help', 'shout hello', 'shout up', 'call out hello' as a shout.
The ledge's wait while the man is away is a sequence keyed on his moves left; the wait at the Vista reads the indicator's clock and says the image stirring.
The table's lean toward the hand is dropped for view IV: the altar's surface 'seems content to be looked at'.

'say hello, sailor' and kin as a greeting, 'wait N' as one move said in character, sleep/rest/nap/wait a while as waits; friction 38/39 status and friction 48 record the dropped remainders for Sprout.
DIAGNOSE says 'You will be cured after N moves.' while wounded.

'pull back hood' and kin as a push; the mist in every shadow room; bare 'search' reads the room; 'feel around' answered; 'dry lamp' and 'dry torch' answered; the endless stair and the Ladder Top's staircase answer 'climb stair' once (without on the composed play).
The Timber Room's narrow way refuses a load by saying it takes nothing bigger than a hand, the light included.
The ship's sailing line adds that he had been listening for something and it was not said.

Tests: the walkthrough extended through the museum, the puzzle (book taken, ladder out), the trip to 776, the ring hidden and found, to 7 of 7 in 208 moves, with seeds that avoid the robot and the guards; every other test's expectations rewritten for the changed prose and re-checked; README brought to three quarters.

intent.md: the round 6 section (every point's change, what Q3 holds and how it is built, the departures: time deaths as the old man's visit, the machine pushed within the museum, one machine per year, the jewels unseen, bare 'machine' a draw), new secrets, and what done looks like for round 6. friction.md: entries 42-52 (verbatim holds no slots; the integer dial role works; a pushed vehicle cannot follow; the pusher must ask the world; a square cannot read its neighbour; a composed play needs without; wait N; three machines one noun; unseen for removed declared things; one of in describe; take all binds the hands) and status notes on 3, 24, 38/39.
